thread:
sam: Quick heads-up — after the AWQ+FP8 changes rolled yesterday we hit OOMs on a 40GB A100 during high-concurrency chat workloads. stack shows cudaMalloc failed when KV cache tried to grow.

maya: Ugh. Any profiler traces? nvtx or cuda-memtrace?

sam: Pasted the short profiler slice: 
```
== PROFILER SLICE ==
time: 2026-01-15T14:02:11Z
peak_alloc: 32.7 GB
total_alloc_ops: 18231
largest_alloc: 4.1 GB (workspace temp)
kv_cache_alloc: 8.4 GB
many_small_allocs: true
nvtx: kernels switching, fallback memcpy around soft-fp8 kernels
error: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation at runtime/allocator.cu:412
```

alex: That `largest_alloc` looks like workspace sizing. Are kernels asking for ad-hoc scratch buffers? We saw similar fragmentation when the allocator couldn't reuse temp buffers because of different alignment/stride requests.

maya: Also check kv cache dtype. Did we default to fp32 for keys/values anywhere after quant change? Mixing fp8 model params with fp32 kv would blow memory.

sam: Confirmed: model params are AWQ (8-bit), but kv cache was still created as `float32` for backward compatibility in the runtime. Changing to `float16` cut peak usage by ~28% in a local repro.

rachel: FP16 KV is fine functionally, but watch precision degradation on very long contexts — we should add a per-model flag to control kv dtype. Also need to ensure math kernels accept fp16 kv without branching to slow paths.

alex: On allocator side, two levers: 1) preallocate a large workspace slab per-device and satisfy temp buffers from that arena (avoid cudaMalloc churn), 2) unify alignment/shape requests via a small set of canonical workspace shapes to increase reuse. Which is cheaper to deploy?

sam: Tried slab prealloc of 6GB earlier — it prevented the OOM but increased steady memory by ~4GB for light workloads (waste). However, it eliminated many small allocs and reduced host<->device memcpy spikes. Tradeoff vs cost.

maya: Suggestion: dynamic slab sizing with low-watermark shrink. Start with small slab, grow on demand, shrink after idle. Add hysteresis to avoid thrashing.

alex: We also need allocator tuning parameters surfaced to Dedicated customers: `workspace_slab_min`, `workspace_slab_max`, `workspace_grow_step`, `enable_zero-copy-reuse` etc. Defaults should be conservative for hosted.

sam: Another regression clue: kernel selector was flipping to a 'compat' kernel for FP8 paths that internally allocated a staging buffer per-thread. That staging buffer wasn't pulled from the global workspace API, so it triggered extra cudaMallocs. PR idea: make all kernels request scratch via platform_workspac e API so allocator can control reuse.

rachel: Agreed. I'll open a PR to standardize kernel scratch API. We should also add a backend assertion in dev builds to fail-fast if a kernel calls `cudaMalloc` during hot path.

deploy-bot: staging deploy queued: staging-2026-01-15-19:03 (contains cursor:rm/workspace-api-standardize).

maya: For quant memory footprint: consider mixed kv strategy — keys stored as `uint8` (AWQ-friendly) and values as `fp16`. Keys are often used for similarity so low-bit may be okay if we dequantize during dot-product. That reduces KV by ~40% in our sims but requires CPU/GPU dequant path and impacts throughput.

alex: Also watch GEMM kernels for mixed-precision pitfalls — some cuBLAS/cuDNN kernels will internally upcast or create temp buffers if input types differ. Need to profile which kernels cause hidden allocations when fed fp8/fp16 combos.

sam: TODOs from thread:
- rachel: PR to standardize kernel scratch API + dev assert for direct cudaMalloc (action: open PR today)
- maya: bench KV dtype combos (fp32/fp16/uint8 hybrid) on 4 model families and report perf/quality tradeoffs (action: run matrix)
- alex: propose allocator config surface and default heuristic (dynamic slab grow/shrink) + perf numbers for hosted vs dedicated (action: doc + perf tests)
- sam: add a quick hotfix in runtime to coerce kv cache default to fp16 when model params are quantized (temporary mitigation)

rachel: I'll pair w/ eng-ml on the correctness evals for fp16/uint8 kv. We should gate on regression tests (long-context retrieval) before flipping defaults.

sam: Thanks — I'll capture the profiler traces and attach to the ticket. For immediate: rolling back the compat kernel switch prevented further OOMs in prod last night. :thumbsup:

maya: sweet. keep rolling notes in the ticket.
